verdict.rationale: iTerm2 ships a built-in LLM chat window. Linked to sessions, it can give context-aware help and run commands on the user's behalf. It requires an optional AI plugin and the user's own API key, and community hands-on use shows it generating commands. The evidence does not document multi-step planning or an explicit per-command approval step. missing for 10: documented approve-before-execute flow, multi-step task planning, in-depth first-party docs on agentic execution, independent corroboration of command execution.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate terminal tasks to a built-in AI agent that plans and executes commands with my approval

citations.quote: Built-in LLM chat window that can optionally interact with terminal contents. Link sessions to get context-aware help, run commands on your behalf, or explain output with annotations.
This is an optional component you can install to enable generative AI features in iTerm2.
